title: Generative Adversarial Networks
overview: A GAN trains a generator and a discriminator in a minimax game. The generator learns to produce samples the discriminator cannot tell from real data.
objectives: Describe the generator and discriminator objectives

method.title: Two players
method.body: The generator maps noise to samples; the discriminator outputs the probability that a sample is real.

method.title: Objective
method.body: The discriminator maximizes classification accuracy while the generator tries to fool it; the non-saturating generator loss maximizes log D(G(z)).

method.title: Alternating updates
method.body: Each iteration updates the discriminator on real and fake batches, then the generator.

method.title: Failure modes
method.body: Training can oscillate or mode-collapse; techniques include spectral normalization and Wasserstein losses.

pseudocode:
for real in loader:
    z = randn(B, dz); fake = G(z)
    loss_D = bce(D(real), 1) + bce(D(fake.detach()), 0)
    update(D, loss_D)
    loss_G = bce(D(fake), 1)
    update(G, loss_G)

playground.starterCode:
import torch, torch.nn as nn
torch.manual_seed(0)
G = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 2))
D = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 1))
bce = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
real = torch.randn(32, 2) + 3.0
fake = G(torch.randn(32, 4))
loss_D = bce(D(real), torch.ones(32, 1)) + bce(D(fake.detach()), torch.zeros(32, 1))
loss_G = bce(D(fake), torch.ones(32, 1))
print("fake shape:", tuple(fake.shape))
print("D loss and G loss computed:", loss_D.item() > 0, loss_G.item() > 0)

quiz.question: Why call fake.detach() when updating the discriminator?
options: To stop gradients from flowing into the generator
